purpose: Clobetasol is a very strong steroid cream, gel, foam, or lotion that you apply to your skin. It is used to treat skin conditions like eczema, psoriasis, and other rashes that cause redness, itching, and swelling. It helps calm down irritated, inflamed skin and brings relief from discomfort.
how_it_works: Clobetasol works by calming down your body's immune response in the skin where you apply it. Think of it like turning down the volume on the inflammation signal your skin is sending out. This reduces redness, swelling, and itching so your skin can start to heal.
common_side_effects: Burning, stinging, or itching right after you apply it. Your skin may become thin over time, especially with long-term use. You might notice stretch marks, skin color changes, or small broken blood vessels in the treated area. Acne or increased hair growth at the application site can also occur.
warnings: Do not use this on your face, underarms, or groin unless your doctor specifically tells you to — it is very strong. Never cover the treated area with a tight bandage or wrap unless your doctor instructs you. Do not use it on children without medical guidance, and keep use short-term whenever possible. Using too much for too long can affect your whole body, not just your skin, because steroids can be absorbed through the skin. Avoid getting it in your eyes.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin area once or twice a day, usually for no more than 2 weeks at a time. Use only a small amount — a little goes a long way with this medication. Your doctor will tell you exactly how often and how long to use it based on your condition. Never use more than directed.
